history.period: 6th century CE claimed in the Madala Panji; architecture suggests 9th century CE (CONFLICT - verify)
history.summary: Located in the southwestern corner of the inner enclosure of the Jagannath Temple complex (west of Rohini Kunda). Vimala is one of the 51 Shakti Peethas - most sources say the navel (nabhi) of Sati fell here (a few say her feet; CONFLICT - verify). The Madala Panji (temple chronicle) attributes the shrine to Yayati Keshari of the Somavanshi dynasty in the 6th century, but the architecture appears 9th century, suggesting a destroyed original rebuilt later; the ASI restored it in 2005. Vimala is the Tantric consort/guardian of Lord Jagannath: cooked food for Jagannath is offered to her before becoming Mahaprasad (only during Durga Puja is separate non-vegetarian food offered to her).

name: Vimala Temple
town_description: Puri is a major coastal city in Odisha on the Bay of Bengal, one of the four Char Dham pilgrimage destinations and home to the Shree Jagannath Temple. It is also known for its beaches, the annual Rath Yatra that draws millions, and the nearby Konark Sun Temple (about 35 km).

travel.road: Inside the Jagannath Temple complex in Puri town; reachable by the same road links as the Jagannath Temple
